2. Written statement on behalf of the aggrieved workman has been filed on 3/0I/2023. Fact of the case 
disclosed in the written statement is that Tanmay Ruidas is a permanent employee of the company and is presently 
posted at Central Hospital, Kalla as Pharmacist since 2/07/209. He came to Central Hospital, Kalla on transfer from 
Sanctoria Hospital of ECL. According to the terms of House Allotment Rules of the company, quarters is provided to 
the employees who are residing beyond five kilometers and House Rent Allowance is to be paid as per the provisions 
of NCWA if quarters is not provided to the employee. Tanmay Ruidas resides at Ruidas Para, Village and PO- 
Pandaveswar, Dist- Paschim Bardhaman which is beyond five kilometers from the place of work. By letter dated 
20/07/20l9 the workman applied before the management to allot quarters to him. Management of ECL without 
allotting quarters stopped payment of House Rent Allowance on his joining the Central Hospital, Kalla. Several 
representations were made by the workman before the management to allot quarters for his accommodation and he

3. The Management of ECL by office order No. ECL/CHK/C-6/Housing/209/279 dated 02//209 allotted 
quarters No. AEQ-4/l] to the workman on temporary basis which was reported by him as not livable. Workman

payment of House Rent Allowance is to the workman from August, 209 is unjustified, illegal and House Rent is

4. Management of ECL contested the case by filing written statement on the same date i.e. 3/0/2023. 
According to the management, workman after joining at Central Hospital, Kalla applied for quarters on emergency

5. Point for consideration is whether the action of the management of ECL in non-payment of House Rent 
Allowance to Tanmay Ruidas from August, 20I9 at Central Hospital, Kalla is justified? If not, to what relief the

6. In order to prove the claim Tanmay Ruidas, aggrieved workman has been examined as Workman Witness-I.

Workman claimed that he is entitled to get House Rent Allowance @ 8% of the basic as per central government

7. To fortify their case, management examined Sh. Raj Narayan Bhattacharjee as Management Witness-I and

handed over the keys to the security department on 25/02/2020. It has been stated in the affidavit that Tanmay Ruidas

quarters. According to the management, repairing of quarters are done after inspection of the quarters and cost 
estimate, budget certification and approval of the competent authority which is a time consuming process. Quarters 
was repaired during the block repairing, done in February, 20l8 and was after wards vacated by Krishan Guin. From 
February, 20I8 to October, 209 the quarters was in a habitable condition but after allotting the same to Tanmay 
Ruidas, he started raising disputes that quarters was not in a habitable condition. In course of examination, the 
management witness produced the following documents: 


(i) Copy of office order dated 02/l/20I9 by which quarters No. AEQ-4/l was temporarily allotted to Tanmay 
Ruidas and he was advised to occupy the quarters and submit occupancy report, is marked as Exhibit M-I. 


(ii) Copy of office order dated 26/2/20I9 by which quarters No. AEQ-I6/l was allotted to Tanmay Ruidas for

(0) Copy of application dated 28/0/2020 of the concerned employee submitted before the CMO(Admn.), 
Central Hospital, Kalla disclosing that due to want of repair he could not occupy the same as there was no water tank 
installed at the quarters and he also claimed for House Rent Allowance for not being allotted a proper quarters, is 
marked as Exhibit M-3. 


(iv) Copy of application dated 05/02/2020 for cancellation of allotment of the quarters as no repairing work was 
done, is marked as Exhibit M-4. 


(v) Copy of declaration dated 25/02/2020 whereby the workman handed over the keys of the quarters No. AEQ- 
6/l, is marked as Exhibit ४-5. 


(vi) Copy of application dated 20/07/20l9 submitted by Tanmay Ruidas for allotment of quarters, is marked as 
Exhibit M-6. 


(vii) Copy of letter dated 2!/03/2009 issued by the General Manager (Admn./Welfare), ECL addressed to CMO 
(I/c), Central Hospital, Kalla communicating that Director (Personnel), ECL in the thirty fifth meeting of Coal India 
Limited Welfare Board Meeting held on 2/04/2007 decided that “payment of House Rent Allowance may be allowed 
in those mines/areas only where there is a shortage of quarters, House Rent Allowance will not be paid if quarters are 
available or allotted but not accepted by the concerned employee” is marked as Exhibit M-7.

After granting opportunity to Tanmay Ruidas to cross-examine the Management Witness, he declined to cross- 
examine and the witness was discharged. 


8. Mr. S. K. Pandey, union representative advancing his argument on behalf of the aggrieved workman stated 
that Tanmay Ruidas, Pharmacist was appointed in the service of ECL on 7/2/204 at Pandaveswar Colliery, ECL. 
He was transferred to Sanctoria Hospital on 9/l2/208 and thereafter was transferred to Central Hospital, Kalla on 
2/07/209. House Rent Allowance of Tanmay Ruidas which he received till he was posted at Sanctoria Hospital was 
stopped on his transfer to Central Hospital, Kalla. Copy of pay slip for July, 20l9 has been produced in support of the 
earlier payment as Exhibit W-8. It is urged that pay slip for the month of September, 20l9 (Exhibit W-9) shows that 
payment House Rent Allowance was discontinued. Workman submitted an application dated 2!/0/208 before the 
management for allotment of quarters (Exhibit W-2). An office order was passed on 02/I!/20l9 (Exhibit W-3) 
whereby quarters No. AEQ-4/l] was temporarily allotted to Tanmay Ruidas with a note that finalization of quarters 
will be done in the next Housing Committee Meeting. It is submitted that quarters No. AEQ-6/! was allotted to the 
employee and he was requested to occupy the same as soon as possible and submit the occupancy report to the Asst. 
Manager (P), Central Hospital, Kalla. No occupation certificate has been produced by the management nor by the 
union. Subsequently, on 28/0l/2020, Tanmay Ruidas submitted an application to the CMO (Admin.), CH, Kalla 
(Exhibit W-5) informing that the allotted quarters was not in a livable condition and that it needs some repair and 
water tank was required to be installed. He also claimed House Rent Allowance since his joining at Central Hospital, 
Kalla with further request that if repairing of quarters and installation of water tank was not done on urgent basis, it 
would not be possible for him to occupy the same. After receipt of letter, management neither repaired the quarters 
and installed the water tank nor did they refute the claim of the workman that no repair was required. It is argued by 
the union representative that an application was submitted by Tanmay Ruidas on 05/02/2020 for cancellation of 
allotment of quarters AEQ-6/l due to non-repair of the same and for payment of House Rent Allowance. Union 
claimed that till date no House Rent Allowance has been paid and the workman is entitled to get House Rent 
Allowance from August, 209 till date. 


9. Mr. P. K. Das, learned advocate for ECL in reply argued that Quarters No. AEQ-4/l was allotted to the 
workman (Exhibit M-|) and thereafter another quarters No. AEQ-6/] was allotted in favour of Tanmay Ruidas but 
the workman did not take possession of it and prayed for cancellation of allotment of quarters on the ground that 
quarters was not repaired (Exhibit M-4). Management relied upon a letter dated 2/03/2009 issued by the General 
Manager (Admin./Welfare) addressed to CMO (I/C), C.H., Kalla (Exhibit M-7) that House Rent Allowance would not 
be paid if quarters are available or allotted but are not occupied by the concerned employee. It was mentioned that 
payment of House Rent Allowance would be allowed in cases if there is a shortage of quarters. It is urged that in the 
instant case, the concerned employee consciously did not take possession of quarters and he is eager to enjoy House 
Rent Allowance. It is argued that the management cannot act contrary to their decision that when quarters are 
available and are not accepted by the employee, he is not entitled to House Rent Allowance. The workman is 
therefore, not entitled to get House Rent Allowance in this case. 


0. I have considered the rival arguments advanced on behalf of the union and Id. Advocate for the management. 
I have also considered the backdrop of the fact and circumstances of this case and rules guiding the employees and the 
management of ECL in respect of payment of House Rent Allowance. Grievance ventilated by the workman is for 
non-payment of House Rent Allowance to him after his transfer to Central Hospital, Kalla w.e.f. l2/07/20I9. It 
appears from the materials on record that Tanmay Ruidas is posted as a Pharmacist at Central Hospital, Kalla bearing 
UM No. 95894. It is gathered from the argument advanced by Mr. S. K. Pandey, union representative as well as 
from Exhibit W-8, a copy of pay slip for the month of July, 209 that workman was receiving House Rent Allowance 
@ Rs. 525.84 per month, prior to his transfer to Central Hospital, Kalla. In paragraph three of the affidavit-in-chief, 
Management Witness has admitted that Tanmay Ruidas is a resident of Pandaveswar and attends duty at Central 
Hospital, Kalla travelling beyond five kilometers from his residence and accordingly he is entitled to get quarters. 
Clause 8..3 of NCWA provides that for the purpose of payment of House Rent Allowance to employees in urban 
areas, government notification or clarification on the subject will be followed as provided in previous agreements and 
shall be applicable from 0/02/202 on the revised basic. Other related issues will be discussed in the standarisation 
committee within a period of three months. Clause 8.l.! provides that existing House Rent Allowance will be @ two 
percent of the revised basic per month w.e.f. 0/02/202 and will be paid to employees who have not been provided 
with residential accommodation. From such settled position between the company and the union, it appears that the 
management is conscious of its obligation to pay House Rent Allowance to its employees who have not been provided 
with residential accommodation. Management relied upon Exhibit M-7, a letter dated 2/03/2009 issued by the 
General Manager (Admin./Welfare), ECL addressed to CMO (I/C), Central Hospital, Kalla, ECL quoting observation 
of the Director (Personnel), ECL on the subject of payment of House Rent Allowance to Wage Board Employees. It 
has been communicated that “In the 357 Meeting of the CIL Welfare Board Meeting held on 27/.04.2007 it was 
decided that ‘Payment of HRA may be allowed in those mines/areas only where there is a shortage of quarters. HRA 
should not be paid if quarters are available, or allotted but are not accepted by the concerned employee.” 


iI. In the instant case, Tanmay Ruidas submitted an application on 20/07/209 i.e. soon after his transfer on 
2/07/209 for allotment of quarters on the ground that his residence is situated thirty seven kilometers away from his

place of work and he was facing difficulties in attending duty. He requested the management for allotment of quarters 
AEQ-5/4 on emergency basis. No action was taken by the management and Tanmay Ruidas submitted his second 
application dated 2/0/209 (Exhibit W-2) praying for payment of House Rent Allowance as per prevailing rules of 
House Rent until allotment of quarters. An office order was passed on 02//209 (Exhibit W-3) whereby quarters 
No. AEQ-4/ll was temporarily allotted to Tanmay Ruidas until finalization of allotment on the next Housing 
Committee meeting. Subsequently, on 9/20.2.20l9 Housing Committee members of Central Hospital, Kalla on the 
basis of meeting held on 7/2/209 allotted quarters No. AEQ-l6/l to Tanmay Ruidas (Exhibit W-4). Concerned 
workman received keys of quarters from the security department but could not occupy the same as it was in a bad 
state of repair and no water tank was installed. Furthermore, quarters was not in a habitable condition. Workman 
requested for necessary repairing of quarters, installation of water tank and payment of House Rent Allowance until 
management makes the quarters habitable. It appears to me that the management being aware of such communication, 
neither took steps for repairing to make the quarters habitable nor did the management respond to the application of 
the workman denying his contention that the quarters required repairing or that there was no supply of water at his 
allotted quarters. The nonchalant conduct of the management goes to establish that grievance of the workman that 
quarters was not in habitable condition and lacked facility of water supply is true and the management did not take 
steps to remedy the same. A mechanical allotment of quarters in whatever condition it may be, cannot compel the 
workman to accept such quarters. Allotment of quarters not in habitable condition is not considered to satisfy the 
decision of the Director (Personnel), ECL that House Rent Allowance would not be paid to employees if quarters are 
available or are allotted but are not accepted. It has not been clarified that quarters should be habitable with basic 
facility of supply of electricity and water for its employees to occupy the same. In the instant case, I find that the 
workman after waiting for a considerable period after his transfer and ultimately submitted an application dated 
05/02/2020 for cancellation of allotment of quarters due to its non-repair and claimed for payment of House Rent 
Allowance. I find from Exhibit W-7 that quarters No. AEQ-6/l was subsequently allotted to Smt. Sujata Biswas, Sr. 
Staff Nurse on 8/06/2020. Therefore, it can safely be held that Tanmay Ruidas was not allotted with any suitable 
quarters for accommodation at Central Hospital, Kalla since his transfer on 2/07/209. Workman, therefore, is not 
disqualified from getting House Rent Allowance on the basis of observation of the Director (Personnel), ECL (Exhibit 
M-7). Accordingly, I hold that action of the management in not paying House Rent Allowance to Tanmay Ruidas is 
unjust, arbitrary and illegal. The management of Central Hospital, Kalla is directed to pay House Rent Allowance to 
Tanmay Ruidas w.e.f. 2/07/209 onwards at the prevailing rates till date. Management shall pay arrear of House 
Rent Allowance to the workman within two months from the date of communication of the Award. 


Hence, 
ORDERED 


that the Industrial Dispute is allowed on contest against the management of Central Hospital, Kalla with a direction to 
pay House Rent Allowance to Tanmay Ruidas at the prevailing rates w.e.f. 2/07/209 till date. Arrear of House Rent 
Allowance shall be paid to the workman within two months from the date of communication of the Award. Let an 
Award be drawn up in the light of my above discussion. Let copies of Award be communicated to the Ministry for 
information and Notification.

] On receiving Order No. L-2202/45/200-IR(CM-II) dated 3/0/20i from the Government of India

2. Union of Koyala Mazdoor Congress filed written statement on 2/02/203 through Mr. H. L. Soni, Asst.

Further case of the union is that Monabala Mondal filed an application before ECL along with a copy of deed of

Mondal and the same was forwarded to the General Manager, Kunustoria Area vide Note Sheet bearing No. 
ECL/PC/P&IR/98/2443 dated 9/09/998. On receipt of Note Sheet and proposal for incorporating the name of Tarun 
Kumar Mondal as adopted son, legal opinion was sought for from the panelled advocate of the company. Mr. P. K. 
Goswami, advocate of the company submitted his legal opinion stating that adoption of Tarun Kumar Mondal by

3. After death of Monabala Mondal, Tarun Kumar Mondal being wholly dependent upon his adopted mother

the claim for employment of the adopted son for which this Industrial Dispute has been raised by the union. 
According to the union, various death benefits of Monabala Mondal like Gratuity, CMPF and LCS amounts have

Mondal and countersigned by the Member of Legislative Assembly have described him as the son of Late Monabala

4. Agent, Parasea Group of Mines, ECL contested the Industrial Dispute by filing written statement on

employment. Management urged that initiating Note Sheet or obtaining legal opinion cannot help in proving that the

valid. Furthermore, there are several irregularities in the claim of adoption made by the union. Management urged that 
the instant case is liable to be dismissed and the concerned person is not entitled to any relief. 

5. Short point for consideration before the Tribunal is whether the action of the management of Parasea 
Colliery, ECL in not providing employment to Tarun Kumar Mondal, claiming to be the adopted son of Monabala 
Mondial, is legal and justified?

7. Facts which transpire from evidence of Workman Witness-I is that alleged adoption of Tarun Kumar Mondal

9. Mr. Rakesh Kumar, union representative advancing argument on behalf of the union submitted that 
Monabala Mondal was a permanent employee of ECL and she died in hamess leaving behind Tarun Kumar Mondal 
as her adopted son. Adoption took place on 25/0/985 with the consent of boys’ family and adoptive parents. Tarun 
Kumar Mondal studied in Jote Janki Free Primary School and in the School Leaving Certificate issued by the Head

Master on 23/0/998 (Exhibit W-6), name of Umapada Mondal, husband of Monabala Mondal appears as father of 
Tarun Kumar Mondal. Referring to the copy of Voter ID card, Ration card and Aadhaar Card, Mr. Kumar submitted 
that in all documents, father’s name of Tarun Kumar Mondal has been recorded as Umapada Mondal. Monabala 
Mondal during her lifetime had made a representation before ECL to incorporate the name of Tarun Kumar Mondal 
as her adopted son but while the management was considering the matter, a legal opinion was sought for from the 
advocate, Mr. P. K. Goswami. Unfortunately, Monabala Mondal died in harness. Tarun Kumar Mondal after death of 
his adoptive mother, submitted application before the management claiming employment as per NCWA but the 
management did not consider the same. It is urged that as per the provision of clause 9.3.3 of NCWA, a legally 
adopted son has to be considered as dependent for employment. In the instant case, adopted son was wholly 
dependent upon earnings of the deceased and the management is duty bound to provide employment to him according 
to NCWA at the earliest. 


0. Mr. P. K. Das, learned advocate in reply argued that Tarun Kumar Mondial is not a legally adopted son of 
Monabala Mondal and he is not entitled to the benefit of employment as per clause 9.3.3 of NCWA. Referring to the 
copy of Service Book of Monabala Mondal (Exhibit M-5) it is submitted that her date of appointment under the 
company was 07/02/995 and in column. No. |7 and 8, name of Tarun Kumar Mondal has been recorded as 
nominee in the capacity of grandson. Referring to the cross-examination of Workman Witness-I dated 02/02/206, Id. 
Advocate argued that the witness clearly stated that Monabala Mondal had no child, therefore, there cannot be any 
scope for Tarun Kumar Mondal to be the real grandson. Witness in his recross-examination stated that he had no 
relationship with Monabala Mondal before his adoption. Therefore, there cannot be any scope for recording the name 
of Tarun Kumar Mondal as grandson. Ld. Advocate for the management further argued that story of adoption has 
been concocted with the sole object to raise a claim for employment under the management by way of false 
representation. It is argued that if any adoption of Tarun Kumar Mondal actually took place on 25/0/I985, at his age 
of four years, why would it take eleven years to execute the deed of adoption on 30/09/997. It is pointed out that 
only after Monabala Mondal was appointed on 07/2/995, process was started to make provision for employment of 
Tarun Kumar Mondal in the capacity of her adopted son. A deed of adoption was prepared with recital that the act of 
adoption took place on 25/0/985. Said adoption was not a valid adoption for the simple reason that Umapada 
Mondal, husband of Monabala Mondal was alive and no adoption can be taken by the wife when her husband is alive 
and not relinquished the world. On perusal of the deed of adoption dated 30/09/997 (Exhibit ७४-।), it appears that the 
alleged adoption took place on 25/0/985 when Tarun Kumar Mondal was four years of age. It implies that adoption 
did not take place for the first time on the basis of deed on 30/09/997, Monabala Mondal passed away after one year 
and one month from the date of execution of the deed of adoption. Claim for employment was therefore initiated even 
before the management of ECL had opportunity of recording the name of Tarun Kumar Mondial as the adopted son of 
the employee. Ld. Advocate for the management on concluding the argument submitted that Monabala Mondal died 
on I/l0/998 i.e. after one year from executing the deed of adoption but at the relevant time, her prayer for 
incorporating the name of Tarun Kumar Mondal had not been allowed. It is urged that the claim for employment of 
Tarun Kumar Mondal is not legally tenable and the Industrial Dispute is liable to be dismissed. 


il. I have considered the fact and circumstances of the case emerging from the respective pleading, evidence 
adduced by parties and argument advanced by the union and the management. It appears from the evidence on record 
that the date of appointment of Monabala Mondal under the employer company was 07/[2/995. It may be gathered 
from School Leaving Certificate of Tarun Kumar Mondal that his date of birth is 07/0/98I. In the voter ID card of 
Tarun Kumar Mondal his date of birth has been recorded as 0/05/98l. Therefore, age of Tarun Kumar Mondal at 
the time of alleged adoption was four years and at the time of appointment of Monabala Mondal on 07/2/995, age 
of Tarun Kumar Mondal would be near about fourteen and half years if the month of May is taken as the month of his 
birth. Therefore, name of Tarun Kumar Mondal certainly would have been described in Column. 6 for recording 
details of her dependents, their relationship and Date of Birth but I find that Column No. 6 of Service Record of 
Monabala Mondal (Exhibit M-5) is left blank. 


2. It would now be prudent to consider the legality of alleged adoption of Tarun Kumar Mondal by Monabala 
Mondal on 25/0/l985. According to the provision of Section 8 of Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act, 956, a 
female Hindu can take in adoption if she is of sound mind, not a minor and not married. If a female Hindu is married, 
she can take in adoption only if her marriage has been dissolved or whose husband is dead or has completely and 
finally renounced the world or has ceased to be a Hindu or has been declared by a court of competent jurisdiction to 
be of unsound mind. In the present case, Monabala Mondal at the alleged time of adopting Tarun Kumar Mondal was 
married and Umapada Mondal, her husband was alive. Therefore, during lifetime of a Hindu married male, his wife 
did not have the capacity to adopt a son or daughter. Therefore, adoption of Tarun Kumar Mondal by Monabala 
Mandal on 25/0/[985 is not a valid adoption. Mr. Indrajit Mukherjee, advocate in his letter dated 08/04/200 
addressed to the Agent, Parasea Colliery (Exhibit M-9) has rightly opined that deed of adoption cannot be treated to 
be legal and valid for the reason that Monabala Mondal having a husband living in the year 985, didn’t have the 
capacity or competence to take any child in adoption.

justified in not providing employment to Tarun Kumar Mondal as the adopted son of Monabala Mondal and the 
Industrial Dispute is liable to be dismissed. 

Hence,

that the Industrial Dispute is dismissed on contest against the union. Tarun Kumar Mondal is not entitled to get

there is no scope for providing employment to the claimant dependent who is now fifty-seven (57) years old. It is 
stated by the witness that once she had exercised the option under Clause 9.3.2 of NCWA she is not entitled to claim 
monetary compensation under Clause 9.5.0 of NCWA. Further case of the management is that the family of the 
deceased employee survived thirty (30) years without any assistance as such she is not entitled to any monetary 
compensation. It is their case that the management is justified in not providing employment and not paying monetary 
compensation from the date of death of her husband. 


7 In course of cross-examination the witness deposed that the claim for employment was processed from 2000 
till 20l5 and she filed relevant documents. It further transpires from his testimony that management did not consider 
her prayer for employment and at the same time no communication was made to Fulmoni Bhuia that she was not 
entitled to any employment. The witness admitted that management received application dated 4.07.20l8 submitted 
by Fulmoni Bhuia praying for monetary compensation and till date management has not considered her prayer for 
monetary compensation and went ahead to deposed that management has not committed any illegality by not 
providing employment and monetary compensation. Copies of the Note Sheets filed by the union representative were 
marked as Exhibit M-3 collectively in three pages on admission. 


8. The moot question to be considered is whether the action of the management in not providing employment 
and not paying monetary compensation to Smt. Fulmoni Bhuia is justified or not? If not, what relief the applicant is 
entitled to. 


9. Mr. Rakesh Kumar, Union Representative argued that the management of ECL deliberately did not consider 
the prayer for employment of the wife of the deceased and no communication was made to her as to the fate of her 
prayer. It is argued that after nearly thirty years from the date of death of Rajdhar Bhuia on 05.2.996, the 
management witness in order to avoid the responsibility of ECL has stated in paragraph no. (I0) of his affidavit-in- 
chief that as the claimant is fifty-seven (57) years old and she is not entitled to employment. Mr. Kumar further 
argued that she claimed employment twenty-nine years earlier and she was much younger by 29 years, eligible for 
employment. At the relevant time management of ECL did not reject her claim for employment but issued a letter 
dated 03/05.2.999 asking her to accept the monetary compensation of Rs. 3000/- (Rupees three thousand only) per 
month in lieu of employment. Mr. Kumar submitted that the management arbitrarily did not process her prayer for 


9]0 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : FEBRUARY 28, 2026/PHALGUNA 9, 947 [PART II—SEc. 3(ii)] 


employment and alternatively tried to impose their decision upon her disregarding her right to exercise option under 
NCWA. It is argued that as the management did not provide her with any employment nor rejected her prayer on any 
plausible ground, the wife of the deceased employment cannot be debarred from claiming monetary compensation at a 
later stage. It is contended that management’s claim that once she opted for employment, she had no right to claim 
monetary compensation, is without foundation and there is no such provision in NCWA debarring the wife of the 
deceased employee from receiving monetary compensation when management deliberately withheld her entitlement 
to employment. Mr. Kumar in support of his argument relied upon the ratio of the decision of the Hon'ble High Court 
at Calcutta in the case of Smt. Shanti Devi Vs M/s. Eastern Coalfields Limited and Others [Writ Petition No. 
2243/2022] where the Hon'ble Court observed that twenty-four years have passed between the death of the 
petitioner’s husband but neither compassionate employment nor MMCC has been given. The whole object of Chapter 
IX of NCWA is on the verge of being frustrated. None of the NCWA applicable to the petitioner’s case has taken 
away the benefits of compassionate employment or MMCC in lieu thereof. The Hon'ble High Court on the aforesaid 
fact and circumstances of the case held that the claim made by the petitioner for MMCC is justified. The ECL is 
directed to pay MMCC to the petitioner at the rate prevailing from time to time from the date of death of her husband 
along with an interest at the rate of three percent per annum. Mr. Rakesh Kumar, referring to Exhibit M-3, a Note 
Sheet dated 26.0.999 argued that the Competent Authority accorded approval to process the case vide Note Sheet 
dated 03/0.09.999 and the age of Fulmoni Bhuia was assessed as thirty years as on |2.!2.997 by the P.M.E Board 
at Jhanjra and she was declared fit. Mr. Kumar strenuously argued that after the conditions for employment were 
found in her favour, the management without rhymes and reasons approved payment of maintenance allowance to the 
dependent wife which they are now denying. 


0. Mr. P. K. Das, learned advocate admitted that the management did not issue any letter, informing the widow 
of the deceased that her prayer for employment was regretted. The only argument advanced by the learned advocate 
for the management is that once the prayer for employment is made and the offer for monetary compensation was 
refused by the wife, her payer for monetary compensation at a later stage could be accepted. It is argued that the 
Industrial Dispute is liable to be dismissed. 


ll. I have considered the rival arguments, the pleadings of the parties, evidence adduced and the relevant 
provisions of NCWA related to payment of monetary compensation to the female dependent of the deceased 
employee. Admittedly, after the death of Rajdhar Bhuia, his wife filed an application before the management for her 
employment. It appears from the document of the management that the claim for employment was made on 
2.0.997 and the Screening Committee of | and 2 Incline, Jhanjra, examined the proposal for employment on 
20.06.997. It appears from the evidence of Mr. Jayanta Gorai (Management Witness No. |) the claim for 
employment was under process from 2000 till the year 20I5. It is also admitted by the witness that the management 
did not consider the prayer for employment and no communication was made to Fulmoni Bhuia after 20I5 that she 
was not entitled to get any employment. Exhibit W-8, a letter issued by Fulmoni Bhuia addressed to the Agent, | and 
2 Incline, Jhanjra Project reveals that the widow of the deceased was expecting her employment on 08.2.20I5 as she 
requested the management to issue necessary direction for processing the employment without further delay and that 
her family members are suffering starvation for the last twelve years. According to Clause 9.5.0 (i) of NCWA-V : In 
case of death due to mine accident, the female dependant would have the option to either to accept the monetary 
compensation of Rs. 3,000/- per month or employment irrespective of her age. 


Clause 9.5.0 (ii) of NCWA-V : In case of death / total permanent disablement due to cause other than mine 
accident and medical unfitness under Clause 9.4.0., if the female dependant is below the age of 45 years, she will 
have the option either to accept the monetary compensation of Rs. 3,000/- per month or employment. In case the 
female dependant is above 45 years of age she will be entitled only to monetary compensation and not to 
employment. 


Clause 9.5.0 (iv) of NCWA-V: Monetary compensation wherever applicable, would be paid till the female 
dependant attains the age of 60 years. 


Clause 9.5.0 (v) of NCWA-V : The rate of monetary compensation which stands at Rs. 2,000/- and Rs. 3,000/- 
per month as mentioned above would be reviewed w.e.f. 0!.07.996. 


2. In the present case the wife of the deceased opted for employment while she was thirty years of age but 
management without refusing her prayer for employment approved payment of monetary compensation to 
Fulmoni Bhuia at the rate of Rs. 3,000/- per month by letter dated 03/05.2.999. Such proposal was initially declined 
by the widow in her letter dated 8.0.2000 (Exhibit M-l). Management of ECL exhibited extreme apathy to the legal 
rights of the dependent wife as well as their obligation towards the family of the deceased. After passage of several 
years when the claim for employment became irrelevant to the aged lady, she has been compelled to turn to her right 
for monetary compensation, only to choose between two odds. The management has exhibited extreme lack of 
fairness, firstly, by not considering the claim for employment in the right prospective as per NCWA and thereafter 
refusing to pay monetary compensation on the basis of an imaginary condition that once the dependent opts for 
employment she is not entitled to monetary compensation. In my considered view the management of ECL cannot 
escape its duty in paying monetary compensation to the dependent wife from the date following the date of death of 


[भाग [ave 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : फरवरी 28, 2026/फाल्गुन 9, 947 9]] 


the workman i.e., 06.2.996 till Fulmoni Bhuia attains the age of sixty years. There is no provision in NCWA that if 
the dependent wife opts for employment she cannot later on opt for monetary compensation. The case of the 
dependent wife is also fortified by the decision of the Hon'ble High Court in the case of Smt. Shanti Devi Vs 
M/s. Eastern Coalfields Limited and Others [Writ Petition No. 2243/2022], where the Hon'ble High Court found 
it justified to direct ECL to pay MMCC to the petitioner at the prevailing rate from time to time from the date of death 
of her husband and the arrear to be paid along with the interest of three percent per annum. It appears to me that long 
delay in paying monetary compensation to the widow has caused immense hardship to the dependent family of the 
deceased employee. The management firstly on account of their indecisive nature and subsequently by their inaction 
has frustrated the legitimate claim of the dependent wife. Furthermore, there has been devaluation of money from 
996 to 2025 in many folds. Therefore, it is appropriate that the management of ECL is directed to pay an interest of 
five percent per annum on the arrear of monetary compensation from the date following the date of death of her 
husband till January, 2026. The management should also pay the monetary compensation at the prevailing rate till the 
wife attains sixty years of age. 


Hence, 
ORDERED 


that the Industrial Dispute is allowed on contest against | and 2 Incline, Jhanjra Project under Jhanjra Area of 
Eastern Coalfields Limited. The management of Eastern Coalfields Limited is directed to pay Monthly Monetary 
Cash Compensation to Fulmoni Bhuia at the prevailing rate from 06.2.996 till she attains the age of sixty years. The 
management is also directed to pay the arrear of maintenance up to 3.0.2026 with interest of five percent per annum 
and also pay the current maintenance from time to time. Let an award be drawn up in light of my above findings. Let 
copies of the Award in duplicate be sent to the Ministry of Labour, Government of India, New Delhi for information 
and Notification.

between the management and the union on 04.08.2009 and accordingly the petitioners were also taken into services of 
the company in the year 20l0 by the management on being identified by the union secretary but subsequently the 
management issued charge sheet on 05.06.20I2 and 06.06.202 respectively against the petitioners on the ground of 
misconduct under clause 26.9 and 26.22 of the Certified Standing Order in which it was alleged that they had 
fraudulently entered into the services of the management by wrongly submitting their documents, certificates, name 
and father’s name in their employment that was a deliberate act which breaches discipline and is subversive of the 
interest of the company. The reply were given to the charge sheets but those were not found satisfactory by the 
management and therefore Enquiry Officers were appointed and enquiry was conducted by them and ultimately the 
Enquiry Officers found the charges against the petitioners proved and then second show cause notices were issued 
and reply of the same were also submitted by the petitioners but that were also not found satisfactory by the 
management and ultimately vide office order dated 0!.04.20l7 the management/Project Officer imposed the penalty 
of dismissal on the petitioners from the services of the CCL with immediate effect on the ground of serious 
misconduct. 


2. Though, the Ld. Counsel on behalf of the concerned workmen has raised the issue of not following the 
principles of natural justice during the enquiry proceeding but as this Tribunal vide order dated 09.0.2020 has held 
the enquiry conducted by the management as fair and proper on preliminary point, that point cannot be re-opened. But 
the Tribunal has to examine whether the penalty of dismissal is legal and justified in the facts, circumstances and the 
materials on record. 


3. On perusal of Ext.M 3 Series in ID No.l9/20l7 and ID No.20/20l7 and Ext.M 2 Series in ID 
No.2/20l7 and 22/20l7 it is evident that on the point of date of birth the petitioners have not adduced any 
matriculation or school leaving certificate or panchayat/municipal birth certificate but they have submitted notary 
affidavits sworn in on 8.0.2009 in which the petitioner Binod Rajak has declared his age as 35 years, Bodhan Rajak 
has declared his age as 34 years, Jyoti Ram has declared his age as 38 years and Dropadi Bai has declared her age as 
33 years and though the original statement of claim or the Award does not speak any specific initial date of joining by 
the workmen but the management has calculated the age of the petitioners since 3]7 March 982 and found the age of 
petitioner Binod Rajak as 7 years, 05 months and 22 days on the date of his initial joining and likewise the age of the 
petitioner Bodhan Rajak has been found as 6 years, 05 months and 22 days, the age of the petitioner Jyoti Ram has 
been found as l0 years, 05 months and 23 days and that of the petitioner Dropadi Bai has been found as 5 years, 05 
months and 2! days on their respective date of initial joining which is not at all practically feasible in view of section 
67 of the Factories Act, 948 which strictly forbids anyone under the age of 4 from working in any factory aiming to 
safeguard children’s health, safety and education aligning with constitutional mandates and international labour 
standard and to prevent child labour and protect children from exploitation in industrial settings. 


4. It further transpires from the above two management exhibits that the age of these petitioners were also 
assessed by medical examination in which their age was ascertained by their appearance which is not legally 
acceptable for want of ossification test as was also rightly submitted by the learned counsel of the petitioners. 


5. As regards the submissions of the learned counsel of the petitioners that there is no basis of the date 3.03.82 
from which the management is calculating the age of the petitioners, he is right because in the statement of claim/WS 
of the workmen of Ref.no.58/92 they have not claimed any specific date from which the workmen initially started 
working but on perusal of the testimony of WW 2 Binod Rajak in Ref. no.58/l992, it is evident that he has been 
working there since 978 and if we calculate his age from the year 978 to 8.0.2009 when he sworn in notary 
affidavit and declared his age as 35 years, his age at the time of initial joining ie in the year 978, comes to 4 years 
only which further complicates the age of the petitioners in this case and makes the story of the petitioners out and out 
impossible. 


l6. Now as regards the contention of the learned counsel of the petitioners that the petitioners were appointed 
by G.M. (P&IR) Head Quarters whereas they were dismissed by the Project Officer who is below the rank of the 
Appointing Authority and so the dismissal is illegal, this Tribunal is of the view that the petitioners who were found 
to be imposters by the CCL and their services were terminated on that basis, can not claim reinstatement merely on 
the ground that the dismissal order was issued by an officer lower in rank than the appointing authority. The 
protection under Article 3l! of the constitution of India which mandates that a person can not be dismissed or 
removed by an authority subordinate to that by which they were appointed, primarily applies to government servants 
ie civil servants whereas the workmen of the company like CCL are governed by the company’s Articles of 
Association and Service Rules and not by the direct constitutional guarantee of Article 3l() in the same manner as 
civil servants. 


Th So in view of the age of the petitioners as declared by them in their respective notary affidavits sworn in 
on 8.0.2009, it is crystal clear that they are not the actual workmen in whose favour the award dated 3.0.96 was 


[भाग ए---खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : फरवरी 28, 2026/फाल्गुन 9, 947 97 


passed by this Tribunal rather their documents appear to have been procured subsequently and they appear to have 
entered in the services of the CCL on those basis which is a serious misconduct being fraudulent and accordingly the 
dismissal order does not appear illegal in the above facts and circumstances of this case. 


8. In the result, on the basis of the above discussed facts, circumstances and materials available on the case 
record, this Tribunal finds and holds that the action of the management in dismissing Sri Binod Rajak (ID-9/207), 
Sri Bodhan Rajak (ID-20/207), Sri Jyoti Ram (ID-2/207) and Smt. Dropadi Bai (ID-22/207) on the ground of 
fraudulent entry into services of CCL, is quite legal and justified and the petitioners are not entitled to get any relief.

New Delhi for information and notification.

0. Heard both sides and perused the materials on record. 


Il. The Ld. Counsel on behalf of the concerned workmen has submitted that all the workmen had been working 
in slurry removal/cleaning work in Rajrappa Coal Washery since 988 regularly and continuously under the direct 
control and supervision of the management and they had been producing goods for the benefit of the management. 
The work of slurry removal is permanent nature of job but they had not been paid by the management their wages as 
per the rate of NCWA in the name of intermediaries namely Asangathit Shramik Sahayog Samittee Ltd. Rajrappa. 
They were not member of that alleged Samittee and they had never worked under the control and supervision of the 
same. The slurry cleaning job was prohibited by the Central Government notification from |.2.990 but even 
thereafter they have been continuously working in slurry removal and therefore they are entitled for regularization. 


2. On the other hand the Ld. Counsel on behalf of the management has submitted that the work of removal of 
slurry from the slurry pond was entrusted on contract basis to the co-operative of persons who all worked by 
themselves. The workers are the shareholders of the co-operative which is called Asangathit Shramik Sahayog 
Samittee Ltd., Rajrappa Washery and the said Co-operative Society is registered under the Co-operative Societies Act 
and it never had so many shareholders/workers as referred to in the reference order and the union has fraudulently 
inflated the number of persons for securing employment for them by unfair means. A contract for removal of slurry 


922 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : FEBRUARY 28, 2026/PHALGUNA 9, 947 [PART II—SEc. 3(ii)] 


was awarded to the above Co-operative Society from 988 to 990 in different spells of the period. The Central 
Government issued notification under section l0 of the C.L.(R&A) Act, 970 in December, 990 prohibiting the 
Category-I of Slurry through the contractors but that was meant for the collieries and are not applicable to coal 
washery. The concerned workmen are the contractor workmen and they have neither been issued the appointment 
letter nor the pay slip nor identity cards by the management and the contractor’s workmen are not entitled to 
regularization. Even after Central Government notification under Section 0 of the C.L. (R&A) Act, 970 the contract 
workers are not entitled to automatic regularization and at last it was prayed to reject the reference and the prayer of

manually from the settling ponds (outside washery) and stacking the same within a radius of 30 Mtrs and WW-3

Co-operative Society and in Paragraph-|0 of his cross-examination he has admitted that he was working since 20.4.88 
and the oral evidence of the workman as well as the agreement and work orders of the different dates goes to establish 
and support the case of the workmen that since the year 988 these workmen have been doing the work of removal of 
slurry from settling ponds of Rajrappa Washery manually and judicial notice is taken to the fact that on l]% 
December |990 the Central Govt. issued a notification u/s 0 of the C.L.(R&A) Act, 970 prohibiting the removal of 
slurry manually by the contract workers and this is also a fact that the work of removal of slurry in a coal washery is a 
perennial and permanent nature of job and after the said notification by the Central Government it became the 
prohibited category of job but the case record shows that even after this notification the Rajrappa Washery continued 
to take this work from the concerned workmen and even after that they are not being paid the wages equal to those of 
the permanent employees. The Hon’ble Supreme Court in case of Steel Authority of India Ltd. & Others Vs. 
National Union Waterfront Workers and others, have been pleased to hold that on issuance of prohibition 
notification under Section 0(]) of the C.L.R.A Act, 970 prohibiting employment of contract labour or otherwise, in 
an industrial dispute brought before it by any contract labour in regard to the conditions of service, the industrial 
adjudicator will have to consider the question whether the contractor has been interposed either on the ground of 
having undertaken to produce any given result for the establishment or for supply of contract labour for work of the 
establishment under a genuine contract or is a mere ruse/camouflage to evade compliance of various beneficial 
legislations so as to deprive the workers of the benefit thereunder and if the contract is found to be not genuine but a 
mere camouflage, the so called contract labour will have to be treated as employees of the principal employer who 
shall be directed to regularize the services of the contract labour in the establishment concerned subject to the 
conditions as may be specified by it for that purpose in the light of Para 6 hereunder and in Para 6 of the said 
judgment it has been held that if the contract is found to be genuine and prohibition notification under section l0() of 
the CLRA Act, 970 in respect of the establishment concerned has been issued by the appropriate government 
prohibiting employment of contract labour in any process, operation or other work of any establishment and where in 
such process/operation or other work of the establishment, the principal employer intends to employ regular 
workmen, he shall give preference to be erstwhile contract labour, if otherwise, found suitable and if necessary, by 
relaxing the condition as to maximum age appropriately taking into consideration the age of the workers at the time of 
their initial employment by the contractor and also relaxing the condition as to academic qualifications other than 
technical qualifications.

Rajrappa Area, Ranchi and M/s. Asangathit Shramik Sahayog Samittee Ltd. Rajrappa as contractor is quite genuine 
and the Central Government has also issued a notification on !" December 990 in respect of the prohibition of 
slurry removal prohibiting the employment of contract labour, it is directed to the management that if he intends to 
employ regular workmen for the removal of slurry he shall give preference to the concerned workmen, if they are 
found otherwise suitable by relaxing the conditions as to maximum age appropriately taking into consideration the 
age of the concerned workmen at the time of their initial employment by the contractor and also by relaxing the 
conditions as to academic qualifications if any. The reference is answered accordingly.

9. Issue 


Whether the demand of the Rashtriya Colliery Mazdoor Sangh that Sri Dilip Kumar and |3 other workers 
(General Mazdoor, Dressers and Sweepers) listed in the annexure, who were removed from service by the 
management of BCCL, Katras Area-4 in 985, be reinstated and regularized in BCCL, is just and proper? If so, to 
what reliefs are the said workers entitled to and from which date? 


0. As regards the oral evidence of the workmen, WW-l Ashok Kumar Singh who is one of the concerned 
workmen, has deposed that he was appointed in the Central Hospital Katras BCCL as Casual Worker on 0.03.983 
for the post of Dresser. Total 22 persons had been working on different posts on casual basis since 0.03.983 and 
they were being paid wages at the rate of Rs. 8.70 per day. They submitted their application to the management of 
BCCL requesting to declare their services as permanent but the management on 9.05.988 declared only 8 persons 
as permanent employee and remaining others were left on the ground that their attendance were less than 240 days in 
a year but the true fact is that none of the workmen including those 8 persons, had completed attendance of 240 days 
in a year. As the management has shown discriminatory policy and violated Articles of law and denied regularization, 
which is totally unjust step taken against them by the management. In the cross-examination he has stated that he was 
working in the BCCL as Casual worker and not as permanent worker. He was paid Rs. 8.70/- per day. He has annexed 
the documents that has details of 22 employees and all of them were working as casual workers and were being paid 
Rs. 8.70/- per day. 


Il. As regards the documentary evidence though all the documents are photo copies but all are important for the 
purpose of this case out of which mark ‘X’ for Identification is the request letter for approval written by Medical 
Superintendent Central Hospital Katras dated 0.0.984 for deployment of casual workers describing that vide note 
sheet dated 7.7.83 approval for deployment of casual workers was given earlier which has been extended up to 
December 984. On its perusal it is evident that the strength of the workers on roll are few in comparison to the

minimum required strength and that is why to run the hospital deployment of casual workers will continue till 
minimum requirement is recruited to maintain cleanliness of hospital as well as day to day work and the names of the 
concerned casual workmen are also mentioned therein. Mark X/I is Proforma for regularization of casual workers 
that contains the names of the casual workers which shows that they were working as sweepers, dressers etc since 
.3.83 and they worked up to 985. Mark X/2 is the letter written by the concerned workmen to the Joint Secretary of

transpires that previously No Dispute Award was passed in this case. Mark X/4 is notary affidavit of Sri Giridhar 
Mishra whch is not legible. Mark X/5 is the copy of order dated 29.08.2023 passed by the Hon’ble Jharkhand High 
Court in L.P.A.No. 28 of 2022 and on its perusal it transpires that the Hon’ble Court have been pleased to set aside 
the award passed by this Tribunal as well as the order of the Hon’ble High Court in W.P. (L) No. 557 of 20l9 and 
this reference has been restored with direction to provide opportunities to the parties to lead evidence and pass an 
award in accordance with law. Mark X/6 Series are the note sheet of the Medical Superintendent dated 06.2.984 
by which the General Manager, Katras Area was requested to extend the approval earlier given for the deployment of 
casual workers in the hospital etc. Another important document of this series is the photo copy of Memorandum of 
Settlement arrived at between the management of Area-IV and Shri L.P. Singh, Secretary, R.C.M.S. on 7.3.988 
and on its perusal it transpires that 8 casual workers who were working as Sweeper in Regional Hospital Katras, after 
it was taken other by the BCCL, they were kept in casual pool of sweepers at Central Hospital Katras for deployment 
as Badli Sweeper against leave and sick vacancy of permanent sweepers in the hospital. 


2. On the other hand १॥५७४-], Rana Santosh Kumar Singh has deposed that in the year 983, BCCL had taken 
over the management of Katras Central Hospital in which 22 casual workers were working at that time out of whom 8 
suitable persons who had complete 240 days attendance in a year were regularized whereas the attendance of Sri 
Ashok Kumar was only II] days and therefore, he was not regularized. In cross-examination he has stated that he 
does not remember the names of all the 22 workers working on casual basis and he also does not remember the names 
of those 8 workers who were regularized. He also does not remember the date of settlement. It has further stated that 
he also does not remember in which year Ashok Kumar Singh has ll days attendance and he also does not 
remember whose attendance out of those 8 suitable persons, was 240 days or above the same. 


3. Admittedly total 22 casual workers were working in Central Hospital Katras some of whom were working as 
Sweeper and others were working as Dresser etc. out of whom 8 casual workmen/sweepers were regularized vide 
settlement arrived at between the management and the union on 7.03.988 but rest l4 casual workers were left and 
not considered for the same. 


4. Now the Management has taken the plea that those casual workers who had completed 240 days attendance 
in a year were regularized as Badli Sweeper and as the other casual workers had not completed 240 days attendance 
therefore, their cases were not considered for the same and in support of the same the management has also given oral 
evidence of ५७- Rana Santosh Kumar Singh who has deposed that the 8 casual workers had completed 240 days 
attendance in a year so they were regularized and the concerned workmen had not completed 240 days attendance in a 
year so they were not considered for regularization but to corroborate the same the management has failed to 
submit/furnish/produce even a single chit of paper which may reveal/prove that 8 casual workers who were 
regularized by the BCCL, had completed 240 days attendance in a year and on the contrary WW-|l Ashok Kumar 
Singh has given his testimony that those 8 workmen had also not completed 240 days attendance in a year which goes 
to prove that the management has adopted pick and choose policy which is illegal. 


I5. Thus on the basis of the above discussions of the facts, circumstances and evidences on record it is crystal 
clear that the Management regularized the services of only 8 casual workmen but left other similarly situated 
workmen which is out and out discrimination and violation of principles of natural justice as well as the spirit of 
Article-l4 and 6 of the Constitution of India. The principle of equality and non- discrimination is the corner stone of 
Indian Labour Jurisprudence. This is settled principle of law that similarly situated workmen can not be discriminated 
solely on the ground that they have not completed 240 days of attendance in a year. 


l6. So in the light of the above this Tribunal comes to the conclusion that all the concerned l4 workmen are 
entitled to be reinstated by the BCCL but it appears that they were stopped from working in the year 985 and now 40 
years have already gone so in the best interest of justice the Management is directed to give compensation of Rs. 
5,00,000/- to each of the concerned workmen within a period of 3 months from the date of publication of the Award. 
The reference is answered accordingly.

ll. On perusal of the entire evidence on record as adduced from the side of the management it is evident that the 
concerned workmen were given employment under Land Loser Scheme on the basis that their land that was acquired 
by the BCCL and in pursuance of their appointment letter they joined in the services of the BCCL as UG. 
Miner/Loader in the year 987 and it further transpires that subsequently about 8 years later ie on 3l.0.995, one 
Munilal Kumhar submitted his representation before the BCCL claiming that 50% of the land belonged to him and 
requested for providing employment against the said land and on verification it was found that Sri MunilalKumhar 
was 50% shareholder of the land in question and thereafter the charge sheets were issued to both the concerned 
workmen i.e. Bishnu Kumhar and Dwarika Kumhar alleging that they have entered into the services of the BCCL 
fraudulently claiming themselves to be the full owner of the land in question that was acquired by the BCCL under 
land loser scheme and thereafter both the concerned charge sheeted workmen submitted their reply that were not 
found satisfactory by the management and enquiry was conducted and on the basis of the enquiry report, ultimately 
both the charge sheeted workmen were dismissed from the services of the company. Though the Ld. Counsel for the 
workmen has contended that the enquiry was conducted without following the principles of natural justice but vide 
order dated 09.2.204 this Tribunal has already held the enquiry as fair and proper which makes it clear that the 
procedure of the enquiry was fair and there is no procedural illegality but despite that the legality or illegality of the 
issuance of charge sheet as well as the dismissal order can still be challenged by a workman and here in the instant 
case on perusal of the entire materials on record it is evident that the management has alleged that concerned 
workmen entered into the services of the BCCL by claiming themselves to be the full owner of the land in question 
whereas they are only the 50% shareholder but in its reply the workmen have repeatedly submitted that they never 
claimed or submitted any application to the effect that they are the full owners of the land in question rather they have 
already admitted that they have only 50% share under the same and the management, though has submitted 
overwhelming documents regarding the enquiry proceeding but has utterly failed to submit even a single chit of paper 
/document either before this Tribunal or during enquiry proceeding itself, which may prove that the concerned 
workmen had ever claimed before the BCCL that they were the absolute/full owners of the land in question and thus 
there is no evidence on record to prove any misrepresentation/misconduct by the workmen or that they ever misled 
the management which breaks down the very back bone of the case of the management and secondly, on perusal of 
Exhibit M-5 as well as Exhibit M-3 it is crystal clear that the management representative, J. Prasad in his cross- 
examination has very clearly admitted that there is no mention in the Circular regarding the quantum of land for 
employment and the same has also been admitted in the cross-examination by MW-|. At the same time, on perusal of 
Rule 6.l(iii) of the copy of Circular No. D(P)/PS/87/l22 dated 03.02.987 of the BCCL it is evident that the quantum 
of land would not be a criteria offering appointment and thus it is crystal clear that there is no specific 
mention/requirement of the quantum of land under the Land Loser Scheme of the BCCL to offer and get employment 
and therefore, in the above facts, circumstances and materials available on the case record, this Tribunal comes to the 
conclusion that as the management has utterly failed to prove any misrepresentation/misconduct by the concerned 
workmen, the issuance of charge sheets dated .2.95 to the concerned workmen as well as the dismissal orders 
dated 9.2.96 passed against them, are itself highly unwarranted and illegal and accordingly the charge sheets are 
hereby quashed and dismissal orders are set aside and it is held that the action of the management of Bhowra (N)

प्रदान किया गया तथा यह वायुसेना मुख्यालय (वायु भवन) की नफरी पर तैनात हैं और 01 फरवरी 2020 से इसरो में प्रतिनियुक्ति पर हैं। 


ये एक लड़ाकू समाघात (फाइटर कॉम्बैट) लीडर, एक एक्सपेरिमेंटल टेस्ट पायलट हैं और गगनयान कार्यक्रम के लिए चुने गए 
चार गगनयात्रियों में से एक थे। 25 जून 2025 को ग्रुप कैप्टन शुक्ला Axiom-4 मिशन के भाग के रूप में इंटरनेशनल स्पेस स्टेशन (ISS) पर 20 
दिन की यात्रा के लिए निडरता और आत्म-विश्वास के साथ आगे बढ़े जो भारत के मानव अंतरिक्ष उड़ान कार्यक्रम के लिए एक मील का पत्थर 
साबित हुआ। ये इंटरनेशनल स्पेस स्टेशन (ISS) पर जाने वाले पहले और चार दशकों से भी अधिक समय अंतराल के बाद अंतरिक्ष की यात्रा करने 
वाले दूसरे भारतीय बने। 


मिशन के दौरान इन्होंने इंटरनेशनल स्पेस स्टेशन (ISS) पर माइक्रोग्रेविटी मानव शरीर विज्ञान तथा एडवांस सामग्री से संबंधित अनेक 
जटिल प्रयोगों को अंजाम दिया। अंतरिक्ष यात्रा से जुड़ी अत्यधिक चुनौतियों तथा खतरों के बावजूद इन्होनें निर्भीकता का प्रदर्शन किया और पूरे 
मिशन के दौरान एकाग्रचित्त रहते हुए संयम बनाए रखा। 


इन्होंने अंतरिक्ष के प्रतिकूल वातावरण में अत्यधिक शारीरिक तनाव, विकिरण प्रभाव तथा मांसपेशियों की क्षति सहित स्वास्थ्य संबंधी 

खतरों, बदली हुई परिस्थितियों के कारण शारीरिक तथा मनोवैज्ञानिक तनाव का सामना करते हुए असाधारण साहस, सहनशक्ति और मानसिक 

दृढ़ता का प्रदर्शन किया। अपनी लंबी अंतरिक्ष यात्रा के दौरान इन्होंने उच्च कोटि की व्यावसायिकता, टीम के रूप में कार्य करने तथा देशभक्ति का 

उदाहरण पेश किया। राष्ट्र के हितों के प्रति Peart प्रतिबद्धता, वैज्ञानिक उत्कृष्टता हासिल करने के प्रति अटल समर्पण तथा चुनौतियों का डट कर 

सामना करते हुए इन्होंने भावी पीढ़ियों के लिए एक शानदार उदाहरण प्रस्तुत किया।

सं. यू-11/2/2022-यूनेस्को--भारत अपनी सांस्कृतिक परंपराओं की अटूट निरंतरता तथा विचार की अनेक धाराओं, सामाजिक संगठन 
और सृजनशीलता को एक साथ समेटने की क्षमता के कारण अद्वितीय है। बहुलता, विविधता, बहुविधता और परस्पर जुड़ाव ऐसे मूल तत्व हैं जिन्हें 
सिद्धांत और व्यवहार, दोनों स्तरों पर कायम रखा गया है। 


वैश्वीकरण और उसके अपरिहार्य परिणामों के संदर्भ में आज इन मूल्यों और सिद्धांतों की प्रासंगिकता और भी बढ़ गई है। वर्ष 2003 के 
'अमूर्त सांस्कृतिक विरासत के संरक्षण पर Hea oT तथा वर्ष 2005 के 'सांस्कृतिक अभिव्यक्तियों की विविधता के संरक्षण और संवर्धन' पर Hea MT 
जैसे अंतरराष्ट्रीय मंचों और संगठनों, विशेषकर यूनेस्को ने स्पष्ट रूप से अपनी चिंता व्यक्त की है। भविष्य के लिए स्थायी मानव व्यवस्था सुनिश्चित 
करने हेतु रणनीतियों के विकास की आवश्यकता पर सक्रिय बहस हुई है। इसका समाधान समेकित सामाजिक-सांस्कृतिक-पारिस्थितिक प्रणाली 
दृष्टिकोण अपनाकर प्रभावी ढंग से किया जा सकता है। 


विभिन्न विषयों और प्रशासनिक संरचनाओं के बीच तथा उनके मध्य समन्वय स्थापित करने, मानव विकास के लिए समग्र दृष्टिकोण की 
आवश्यकता के प्रति राष्ट्रीय जागरूकता उत्पन्न करने और इसके विभिन्न आयामों को एकीकृत करने के उद्देश्य से, भारत सरकार ने निम्नानुसार

No. 15-Pres/2026—The President is pleased to approve the award of the “Ashoka Chakra” to the under mentioned 
personnel for the act of daring and most conspicuous bravery: — 


1. 29014, GROUP CAPTAIN SHUBHANSHU SHUKLA, FLYING (PILOT) 
(Effective date of Award: 25 June 2025) 


29014, Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla was commissioned as a fighter pilot in the Flying branch of the IAF on 17 
Jun 2006 and is on the posted strength of Air HQ (VB) and on deputation to ISRO with effect from 01 Feb 2020. 


He is a Fighter Combat Leader, an Experimental Test Pilot and was chosen as one of the four Gaganyatris for 
Gaganyaan programme. On 25 June 2025, as part of the Axiom-4 mission, Group Captain Shukla boldly embarked on a 
20-day journey to the International Space Station (ISS), marking a historic milestone for India's human spaceflight programme. 
He became first ever Indian aboard ISS and the second Indian to travel to space after a gap of more than four decades. 


During the mission, he undertook a series of complex experiments on board ISS, dealing with microgravity, human 
physiology, and advanced materials. In spite of the immense challenges and risks associated with space travel, he displayed 
unflinching courage, remaining focused and composed throughout the mission. 


He displayed exceptional courage, resilience and mental fortitude in the hostile environment of space, coping up with 
profound physical stress, radiation exposure, and health risks including muscle loss, altered physiology and psychological 
stress. During his space odyssey, he exemplified the highest standards of professionalism, teamwork, and patriotism. His 
selfless commitment to the nation's interests, unwavering dedication in pursuit of scientific excellence, and his unshakeable 
resolve in the face of challenges, have set a shining example for generations to come. 


For his most conspicuous bravery, Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla is awarded ‘Ashoka Chakra’.

On 19 September 2025, he was tasked to drive the TATA 407 vehicle deployed with COB Nambol for movement of 
a section led by Naib Subedar Shyam Gurung, for flood relief operations in Imphal Valley, Manipur. After completion of said 
task, while returning to COB Nambol, the vehicle was ambushed by unknown Imphal Valley Based Anti-National Elements at 
Nambol Sabal Leikai on National Highway 2 in Bishnupur district at 1740hrs. Rifleman Dhurba Jyoti Dutta was driving the 
vehicle, while Naib Subedar Shyam Gurung was in the co-driver’s seat. Nine Other Ranks were in rear compartment of the 
vehicle. In the initial burst, Naib Subedar Shyam Gurung was hit on the neck by a bullet and immediately succumbed to the 
injury. Rifleman Dhurba Jyoti Dutta himself sustained multiple gunshot wounds on his thigh, chest, shoulder and forearm. 


Despite being grievously injured and vehicle tyres being punctured, he sensed the grave danger to his comrades. 
Maintaining composure and displaying exemplary presence of mind, Rifleman Dhurba Jyoti Dutta drove the vehicle out of the 
Killing Zone of the Ambush, under intense hostile fire. His bravery and swift actions, with disregard to personal safety, saved 
the lives of eight fellow soldiers travelling in the rear compartment of the vehicle. 


For his gallant actions and operational excellence, Rifleman Dhurba Jyoti Dutta is awarded “SHAURYA CHAKRA”. 
11. 08030Z LIEUTENANT COMMANDER DILNA K 
(Effective date of Award: 26 January 2026) 


Lieutenant Commander Dilna K was selected for Navika Sagar Parikrama वीं, a pioneering dual-handed 
circumnavigation abroad INSV Tarini. Between 02 October 2024 and 29 May 2025, she sailed over 25,600 nautical miles 
through the Indian, Pacific, Atlantic and Southern Oceans, braving isolation, extreme weather and technical challenges. In the 
Pacific, the vessel suffered total power failure, disabling critical systems and demanding manual navigation under high-risk 
conditions. While navigating through the perilous Drake Passage in stormy conditions that caused the boat to heeled severely. 
Regaining control required exceptional skill and extraordinary courage in the face of nature’s raw fury. In both incidents, her 
technical skill, composure and resilience were critical in restoring stability and safety. 


During the expedition, she alongwith her crew became the first Indians to reach Point Nemo-the oceanic Pole of 
Inaccessibility by sailboat. The dual-handed format required 24X7 readiness, navigation, maintenance and emergency 
responses. Despite fatigue, equipment failures and life-threatening seas, she displayed unwavering courage, seamanship and 
leadership. Her fearless conduct, professionalism and resolve under dire conditions reflect the highest standards of Naval 
service. 


For her exemplary endurance, bravery and devotion to duty in this unprecedented expedition, Lieutenant Commander 
Dilna K is awarded Shaurya Chakra. 


12. 09134H LIEUTENANT COMMANDER ROOPA A 
(Effective date of Award: 26 January 2026) 


Lieutenant Commander Roopa A was selected for Navika Sagar Parikrama II, a dual officer circumnavigation of the 
globe aboard INSV Tarini. Over 238 days from 02 October 2024 to 29 May 2025, she sailed over 25,600 nautical miles across 
four oceans-including Cape Horn and the treacherous Drake Passage, where violent storms and strong currents nearly capsized 
the vessel. During the Pacific leg, a complete power failure left the crew without navigation and communication equipment, 
requiring manual operation and traditional seamanship in vast isolation. Her ability to stay composed lead decisively and restore 
critical systems showcased exceptional skill and resolve. She along with her crew also became one of the first Indians to reach 
Point Nemo by a sailboat. 


The mission demanded constant watch keeping, equipment repair, resourcefulness and calm leadership in life- 
threatening conditions repeatedly made the difference between mission success and disaster. Her steadfast courage, operational 
excellence and unyielding spirit in the face of grave adversity reflect the finest traditions of the Indian Navy. 


In recognition of her gallant action in trying circumstances in the face of life and death, Lieutenant Commander Roopa 
A is awarded Shaurya Chakra.

13. 129078 ASSISTANT COMMANDANT VIPIN WILSON, 20 BN, CRPF 
(Effective date of Award: 11 November 2024) 


On 11 Nov 2024, near at Borobekra area of Distt Jiribam, Manipur, sentry observed some suspicious moment. Later, 
a powerful blast was heard, followed by heavy automatic fire from armed insurgents. Two insurgents advanced towards the 
LMG Morcha of platoon post D/20 Bn in an attempt to overrun it and 3- 4 insurgents occupied the mortar pit near the platoon 
post Main Gate with heavy firing on sentry posts. Another insurgent group launched a coordinated attack on D/20 Bn Camp 
and PS Borobekra to divert the response of forces. 


Shri Vipin Wilson, AC ensured to coy personnel are in defensive positions and mobilized his QAT in bulletproof 
Rakshak vehicle and rushed to reinforce the embattled Platoon Post. The QAT came under intense fire power by hidden 
insurgents in houses and paddy fields. He commanded QAT to maintain exemplary composure under firing and coordinated 
accurate retaliatory fire, and ensured that his team broke the ambush even though vehicle hits with multiple bullets. Despite 
this, he courageously dismounted under continuous gunfire, took position behind the vehicle bonnet, and delivered precise 
retaliatory fire power. He again displayed outstanding courage by re-entering the vehicle, directing tactical manoeuvres and 
leading a second advance toward the Post. He engaged insurgents through steady and accurate fire and forced the attackers to 
retreat overrunning the defensive positions. He advanced alone, closed to insurgent-held position, and neutralized the hardcore 
insurgent, recovering critical weaponry. Under sustained enemy fire, he led the first group of pronged, tactical assault resulted 
in the elimination of ten heavily armed insurgents and recovery of a large cache of weapons. He demonstrated outstanding 
battlefield judgment and led from the front with exceptional bravery. 


For displaying extraordinary courage, selfless devotion to duty, and inspirational leadership under the most 
challenging combat conditions, Shri Vipin Wilson, AC of 20 CRPF, is awarded with “Shaurya Chakra” on the occasion of RD 
2026.

RESOLUTION 
Coordination Committee on the Living and Diverse Cultural Traditions of India 


No. U-11/2/2022-UNESCO—India is unique for its unbroken continuity of cultural traditions and its capacity to hold 
many worlds of thought, social organization and creativity together. Plurality, diversity, multiplicity and inter-connectedness 
are principles which have been sustained at the level of both theory and practice. 


These values and principles have a renewed relevance today in the face of globalization and its inevitable 
consequences. International forums and organizations, principally UNESCO, have unambiguously voiced their concern e.g. in 
the Convention of 2003 for the Safeguarding of Intangible Cultural Heritage and the Convention of 2005 for the Protection and 
Promotion of the Diversity of Cultural Expressions. There has been an active debate on the need to evolve strategies to ensure 
a sustainable human order for the future. This can be effectively addressed by adopting an integrated socio-cultural-ecological 
systems approach. 


With a view to establishing a synergy between and amongst different disciplines and administrative structures, to 
create a national awareness on the need for a holistic approach to human development, and integrating its various dimensions, 
the Government of India has resolved to set up a Coordination Committee on the Living and Diverse Cultural Traditions of 
India, as under:—

Il. Terms of Reference of the Committee:— 


1. 


To flag issues of the contemporary situation where there is imminent danger of many of the languages, 
knowledge systems, craft production and craft traditional technologies becoming extinct. 


To suggest linkages between the fluid world of traditional knowledge systems, cultural expressions and 
the variety of production and the more structured world of formal study. 


To suggest systemic changes so as to create space and opportunity for a meaningful synergy/dialogue 
between the domains of traditional knowledge systems, specially in the disciplines such as astronomy, 
mathematics, medicine, metallurgy and 'modem’ science, technology. 


To address the issues of integrating traditional knowledge, skills and values into the formal system of 
education at elementary, secondary and tertiary levels and the institutions in the domains of Science and 
Technology. 


To coordinate activities for the relevant UNESCO Conventions (the Safeguarding of intangible Cultural 
Heritage and the Protection and promotion of the Diversity of Cultural Expressions) and 
Agreements/MoUs with other multilateral agencies and groupings such as BIMSTEC that concern India's 
Living Heritage. 


To initiate the process to build up a knowledge corpus of India’s ethno- knowledge practices, such as 
ethnobotany, ethnoagriculture, ethnomedicine, traditional architectural technologies and the entire range 
of oral (or indigenous) languages. 


To evolve an innovative and appropriate database to authentically record the extensive and diverse range 
of India’s traditional knowledge system so that it reflects the adversity of the natural, cultural and human 
landscape. 


To suggest measures to ensure a digital presence on the web so that the richness of the Living and Diverse 
Cultural Traditions of India is displayed to the world and becomes available to cultural producers 
everywhere. 


This issues with the approval of Hon’ble Minister of Culture.

2. समिति के कार्य :-- 


इस समिति का कार्य राजभाषा विभाग, गृह मंत्रालय द्वारा निर्धारित नीतियों के अनुसार खाद्य प्रसंस्करण उद्योग मंत्रालय तथा इसके 
प्रशासनिक नियंत्रणाधीन स्वायत्तशासी शिक्षण संस्थानों में हिंदी के प्रगामी प्रयोग से संबंधित विषयों पर आवश्यक सलाह देना होगा। 


3. कार्यकाल:-- 

समिति का कार्यकाल सामान्यतः: इसके पुनर्गठन की तारीख से निम्नलिखित शर्तों के अधीन तीन वर्ष तक होगा, बशर्ते कि:-- 
(क) जो संसद सदस्य इस समिति के सदस्य हैं, वे संसद सदस्य न रहने पर इस समिति के सदस्य नहीं रहेंगे । 

(ख) समिति के पदेन सदस्य अपने पद पर कार्य करते रहने तक समिति के सदस्य होंगे | 


(ग) यदि किसी सदस्य के त्याग पत्र, मृत्यु आदि के कारण कोई स्थान रिक्त होता है तो उस स्थान पर नियुक्त सदस्य तीन वर्ष के 
कार्यकाल की शेष अवधि के लिए ही सदस्य होगा | 


4. सामान्य 


समिति का मुख्यालय नई दिल्‍ली में होगा। माननीय प्रधानमंत्री जी की अध्यक्षता में गठित केन्द्रीय हिंदी समिति की दिनांक 06.09.2018 
को हुई 31वीं बैठक में लिए गए निर्णय के अनुसरण में राजभाषा विभाग, गृह मंत्रालय के दिनांक 21.01.2019 के कार्यालय ज्ञापन 
सं. 14013/01/2019 - रा.भा. (नीति) के अनुसार हिंदी सलाहकार समिति की बैठक का आयोजन दिल्ली क्षेत्र में किया जाना अपेक्षित है। 


5. यात्रा तथा अन्य भत्ते 


समिति की बैठकों में भाग लेने के लिए गैर-सरकारी सदस्यों को राजभाषा विभाग के दिनांक 22 जनवरी, 1997 के कार्यालय ज्ञापन 
सं. ॥/20034/4/86-रा.भा.(क-2) में निहित दिशानिर्देशों के अनुरूप और भारत सरकार द्वारा समय-समय पर यथासंशोधित निर्धारित दरों एवं 
नियमों के अनुसार यात्रा भत्ता और दैनिक भत्ता दिया जाएगा । 


आदेश 


आदेश दिया जाता है कि इस संकल्प की प्रति समिति के सभी सदस्यों, भारत सरकार के सभी मंत्रालयों तथा विभागों, राष्ट्रपति 
सचिवालय, उप राष्ट्रपति सचिवालय, प्रधान मंत्री कार्यालय, मंत्रिमंडल सचिवालय, संसदीय कार्य मंत्रालय, लोक सभा सचिवालय, राज्य सभा

4. And whereas, the Registrar, Vels Institute of Science, Technology and Advanced Studies (VISTAS) (Deemed to be 
University), Tamil Nadu, vide letter No. VISTAS/R/MoE/085/2025 dated 15.09.2025, submitted compliance report in respect

G.S.R. 63.—In exercise of the powers conferred by the proviso to article 309 of the Constitution and in 
supersession of the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (Librarian) Recruitment Rules, 2008, in so far as they relate to the 
post of the Librarian, except as respects things done or omitted to be done before such supersession, the President 
hereby makes the following rules regulating the method of recruitment to the post of Librarian in the Income Tax 
Appellate Tribunal, namely:- 


1. Short title and commencement.- (1) - These rules may be called the Income-tax Appellate Tribunal, Library 
and Information Assistant (Group “B’ Posts) Recruitment Rules, 2026. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 


2. Number of posts, classification and level in pay-matrix.- The number of the said post, its classification and 
level in the pay-matrix attached thereto shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the Schedule annexed to these 
10165. 


3. Method of recruitment, age-limit, other qualifications, etc.- The method of recruitment, age-limit, 
qualifications and other matters relating to the said post shall be as specified in columns (5) to (13) of the said 
Schedule. 


4. Disqualifications.- No person, - 

(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or 

(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person, 
shall be eligible for appointment to the said posts: 


Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal law 
applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing, exempt any 
person from the operation of this rule. 


3: Power to Relax.- Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do, it 
may, by order and for reasons to be recorded in writing and in consultation with the Union Public Service 
Commission, relax any of the provisions of these rules with respect to any class or category of persons. 


6. Saving.- Nothing in these rules shall affect reservation, relaxation of age-limit and other concessions required 
to be provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes, ex-Servicemen and other 
special categories of persons, in accordance with the orders issued by the Central Government from time to time in 
this regard.
